summary: Australia records whether victims and offenders are Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander, with official rates, but everyone else is 'non-Indigenous', so White or European-descent Australians are never separately identified. Police victim data by Indigenous status cover only NSW, Queensland and South Australia; offenders are not linked to child victims; trafficking and online exploitation have no heritage data.

nations.Federal (ABS, AIHW, AFP): National police-recorded crime statistics, child-protection data and homicide monitoring, with Indigenous status.
nations.States and territories: Police and child protection are state-run; Indigenous status in crime data meets ABS standards only in some states.

groups.label: Non-Indigenous (White and all other groups combined)

european_title: Not separately identified by any Australian official source
european_note: Australian official statistics record Indigenous status (Aboriginal, Torres Strait Islander, or both) and sometimes country of birth. Everyone else is 'non-Indigenous', which combines White Australians with Asian, Middle Eastern, African and all other Australians, so European descent cannot be identified for victims or offenders.

victims.rate_label: victims per 100,000 children of the same group
victims.rate_note: Official ABS victimisation rates (Tables 11 and 26/24). No rate is published for non-Indigenous children separately.
victims.share_note: Indigenous status is self-identified when recorded by police. 'Non-Indigenous' (and the all-children rate) includes White Australians together with every other group, so European-descent children are not separately identified. Published only for NSW, Queensland and South Australia, where data quality meets ABS standards. Share calculated here: 1196 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander victims of 7095 victims aged under 18 at report in NSW; the total includes victims whose Indigenous status was not stated (about one in ten for sexual assault, all ages).

components.name: Victim heritage
components.full: Official data by harm that separately identify children of European descent (e.g. White non-Hispanic, White British) alongside every other group, self-reported or official, few unknowns. Broad categories that lump European-descent people with others get partial credit; proxies (nationality, citizenship, migration background, country of birth) at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Perpetrator heritage
components.full: Same standard for perpetrators: not perceived, few unknowns, European descent separately identified. Proxies at most 9.4 points.

components.name: Coverage and missing data
components.full: Over 90% of the population covered, under 10% unknown

components.name: Rates and linkage
components.full: Rates per 100,000 possible, and victim heritage linked to perpetrator heritage

score.gold_standard: 100% means a country publishes data that separately identifies people of European descent, both as perpetrators (so one can tell when they disproportionately harm a group) and as child victims (so one can tell when European-descent children are disproportionately harmed), alongside every other group, linked victim to perpetrator, for every harm.
score.rules: Heritage is 75 of every 100 points (victims 37.5, perpetrators 37.5); coverage, rates and access share the other 25. Proxies such as nationality or migration background earn at most a quarter of the heritage points. A country with no real ethnicity data for victims or perpetrators is capped at 25%.
score.why: Australia scores 20% on the stricter scale (20-40%). Its police and child-protection data identify Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children and offenders, often with official rates, but everyone else is counted as 'non-Indigenous', so White or European-descent Australians are never separately identified. Police Indigenous data cover only some states, offenders are not linked to child victims, and trafficking and online exploitation carry no heritage at all.
score.judgement_notes: Indigenous status is real ethnicity data, so the 25% cap does not apply, but every side is binary and lumps White Australians with all other non-Indigenous people, so heritage credit is kept low (at most 9 of 37.5). Police data cover only NSW, Qld and SA for victims. If Indigenous-only data were treated as no European-descent data and capped, Australia would still score about 20%, because it is already below the cap.
